subject: OpenFlux weights distribution & publisher onboarding
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@openflux.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo last week. OpenFlux's 7B/13B weights looked promising for a number of our mid-market customers who need high-quality local hosting. We'd like to propose adding OpenFlux models to Redwood's Partner Catalog (publisher distribution) and would like to align on the following high-level items before we send a formal onboarding packet:

- Distribution model: hosted via Redwood catalog (we serve), or weights escrow + private deployment (customer self-hosting)?
- License terms we would surface to customers (attribution, redistribution rights, commercial use)
- Rev share / revenue model (if Redwood hosts and charges access fees)
- Embargo/early access — do you want a delay window for public redistribution?
- Technical checklist: quantization compatibility, sharded weights, and checksum/attestation workflow

I've attached a short draft of partner terms to orient the conversation (draft_partner_terms_openflux_v1.pdf). If this looks good, Camila and I can coordinate an onboarding timeline and legal review.

Would you be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through options?

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[attachment: draft_partner_terms_openflux_v1.pdf]

From: Alice Park <alice@openflux.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: OpenFlux Legal <legal@openflux.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Hi Grace —

Appreciate the outreach — excited by the possibility. Quick answers up front:

- We prefer Redwood to host in-catalog where possible (simpler for customers) but will consider an escrow/private-host option for higher-risk/regulatory customers.
- Attribution is fine; redistribution needs to be controlled (no blanket downstream rehosting).
- Rev share: we typically ask for a baseline 20% of gross for hosted access, flexible for committed volume.
- Embargo: we usually request a 30-day commercial embargo after initial release to coordinate PR and partner activations.

I've looped in our legal contact to handle specific licensing language — Ben (cc'd on the next reply) will share redlines. We're available for a sync tomorrow at 11am PT.

Best,
Alice
Head of Biz Dev, OpenFlux Labs

From: Ben Cho <ben.cho@modelworks.ai> for OpenFlux Legal <legal@openflux.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Alice Park <alice@openflux.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Hi all —

I'm Ben, counsel for OpenFlux. Thanks for sharing the draft. A few items we will want to capture in any partner distribution agreement:

1) License scope: we prefer a non-exclusive commercial license to Redwood for distribution and hosting, with explicit prohibitions on sublicensing the raw weights for redistribution. Customers can use models commercially but cannot publish the raw weight files.
2) Escrow & verification: for customers requesting on-prem/private deployments, OpenFlux requires an attestation flow and a cryptographic checksum to ensure integrity of weights; we expect Redwood to maintain a signed transfer log.
3) Export controls & sanctions: standard compliance language — we need the same KYC/checklist you already use.
4) Indemnity and limits: OpenFlux prefers carve-outs around data-trained IP claims; we will propose mutual indemnities with a capped liability.
5) Rev share accounting: request quarterly statements and a 45-day payment term.

I've attached a redline that maps our starting position (redline_partner_terms_openflux_v1.docx). We are broadly open to the 30-day embargo but would like a defined marketing calendar.

Ping me with any clarifying questions; Camila/Laura, if Redwood has a preferred clause set, please share so we can converge quickly.

Regards,
Ben Cho (on behalf of OpenFlux Legal)
[attachment: redline_partner_terms_openflux_v1.docx]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Ben Cho <ben.cho@modelworks.ai>, Alice Park <alice@openflux.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Thanks Ben — helpful notes. From an onboarding / ops perspective, here's the playbook we'd use (high level):

- Step 1 (Legal): Agree on partner terms + embargo window + rev share cadence (target 2 weeks).
- Step 2 (Tech intake): OpenFlux submits a package (weights, checksum, quantization guidance, sample inference code). We run an internal compatibility sweep and produce a "compatibility profile".
- Step 3 (Staging): Redwood hosts a staging endpoint (non-billable) for partner QA for up to 14 days.
- Step 4 (Launch): Coordinate PR/marketing calendar inside the agreed embargo. We flip to public catalog and enable billing.

Jonas — can your team confirm the typical time to run a compatibility sweep for a 7B/13B model (quantization tests, KV cache validation)? And Laura — we can take Ben's redlines and propose a short counter; do you want me to coordinate a tracked doc?

We also maintain a short publisher-onboarding-checklist.csv (attached) that lists artifacts we need from the publisher — makes the intake much faster.

Proposed sync: 11am PT today (same slot Alice suggested). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

- Camila
Senior Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
[attachment: publisher-onboarding-checklist.csv]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Cho <ben.cho@modelworks.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Hi Ben / team —

Thanks for the redline. A few points from Redwood legal to speed convergence:

- Sublicense carve: Redwood will not distribute raw weights; we prefer language that allows Redwood to host binaries and provide model access APIs. We can accept a prohibition on publishing raw weights but need the right to serve the model in our hosted catalog.
- Indemnity: Redwood requests mutual IP indemnities except where a party has materially modified artifacts. We will propose a cap tied to annual revenues for the relevant product line.
- Escrow/attestation: happy to adopt an attestation log. Redwood prefers an automated checksum + signed manifest workflow; we can operationalize this via our ingestion pipeline (automated receipts).
- Accounting: 30-day payment on rev-share with quarterly reporting (Redwood prefers shorter cadence for cashflow).

Camila — please send the editable counter; I will prioritize review. If we can close legal terms this week we can likely onboard staging in early December.

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Park <alice@openflux.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@modelworks.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner distribution: OpenFlux model weights availability

Thanks everyone — this is a productive thread. Quick confirmation:

- 11am PT sync accepted (joining via Google Meet link in the invite).
- OpenFlux will accept Redwood-hosted API access as the primary distribution mode for general customers; escrow/private-hosting available for named accounts under separate SOW.
- Ben will update the redline with a narrower indemnity carve and export compliance language; expect update by EOD.

We look forward to the sync and getting the onboarding checklist completed.

Best,
Alice
Head of Biz Dev, OpenFlux Labs
